summary: The Phase 2 artifact is a credible visual and interaction shell with bundled recorded piano assets, shared note routing, and a connected Web Audio graph. It passes the supplied verification checks, but its visual geometry is substantially too wide/short, the Piano behavior is only partially wired, audio-boundary tests are absent, and several claimed controls do not alter the audible graph. MIDI is truthfully shown as denied in the live browser.

evidence: The live 1440x900 render preserves the broad Stage 4 88 concept: continuous red chassis, six ordered regions, dark inset control plates, two OLEDs only in Program and Synth, and 88 A-to-C keys.

Against the supplied reference, the instrument is visibly too wide and shallow; the candidate CSS fixes the instrument at aspect-ratio 3.71/1, while the reference product silhouette is approximately 3.1/1.
The render replaces much of the photographed control density/material detail with small repeated generic knobs/buttons and omits many exact section landmarks.
The live 390x844 render keeps the red chassis continuous, keeps all 88 keys inside the end cheeks, and uses a horizontally scrollable control deck rather than clipping the instrument itself.

Desktop content is fully visible without vertical scrolling, and the narrow render remains contained, but only the first few panels are visible at once and the compressed keybed/control typography is difficult to use at narrow width.
Live pointer interaction and computer-keyboard interaction were exercised successfully; pressed-key classes update and release through the shared App handlers.
Keyboard buttons use pointer events, which covers touch-style pointer input, and the source has an injectable MIDI parser/connection boundary.
The live browser reported MIDI DENIED, so physical MIDI input was not demonstrated; the computer-key map covers only a 16-note subset.
The Piano panel exposes layer levels, type buttons, model selection, touch curves, dynamic compression, timbre, soft release, string resonance, sustain, unison, and acoustic controls.

Type/model/touch and several toggles update canonical Piano state and the Program OLED, but layer levels are not applied to the audio layer gains; piano-timbre-control and piano-acoustics are decorative state; zones/octave shift, list modes, pedal-specific UI, and missing-model selection are not implemented.
The supplied feature matrix points audio requirements at src/audio.ts rather than dedicated audio tests, and no src/audio.test.ts, pianoEngine.test.ts, pianoState.test.ts, or midi.test.ts exists.
The live render shows the correct two primary OLED locations; the Program OLED changes for type/model and Live program selection, and the footer/status reports SAMPLED PIANO and MIDI DENIED.
The source includes a Piano not found display path and a labeled FALLBACK · SYNTH PIANO status, but the UI has no exercised missing-model path and the Synth OLED is static.
IMPLEMENTATION_DETAILS.json identifies seven bundled VSO2/Tone.js Instruments MP3 recordings under public/audio/piano, with source and CC BY 3.0 license, and the live browser reported SAMPLED PIANO.

The engine nearest-root rate-shifts only seven A-root samples and documents a single recorded velocity layer, so it is credible recorded material but not the broad root/velocity coverage described by the manual.
PianoAudioEngine implements noteOn, noteOff, repeated-note replacement, 32-voice limiting, deterministic oldest/released voice stealing, allNotesOff, release envelopes, and ended/timer cleanup.

The live pointer/computer key path reaches these handlers, but no real audio-output or OfflineAudioContext lifecycle test was present; when Web Audio context creation returns null, noteOn immediately returns null despite the fallback label.

Velocity reaches gain, touch curves alter velocity shaping, dynamic compression changes compressor parameters, timbre changes a high-shelf filter, soft pedal changes layer gain, and master volume/reverb are connected to the graph.

String resonance is carried in params but does not alter the graph; unison only changes playback rate by 0.2% per level rather than adding voices; layer level state, Piano timbre/acoustics knobs, and several panel controls do not reach audio.
The engine supports sustain values, deferred release, a half-pedal numeric value, a global sostenuto flag, 32 concurrent voices, and deterministic stealing.

Sostenuto is implemented as a global boolean rather than capturing only notes held at pedal-down; MIDI sustain toggles the React sustain state regardless of whether the incoming CC value is pedal-up or pedal-down; soft-pedal/sostenuto UI and dedicated per-note tests are absent.
Live pointer and mapped computer-keyboard playability worked, key depression/release is visibly reflected, and rapid lifecycle support exists in the engine.
Touch is only indirectly covered through pointer events, MIDI could not be exercised because the browser denied permission, and the mapped computer keyboard exposes only 16 notes.

Live controls expose accessible names/roles, knob arrow-key changes update aria-valuenow and visual rotation, buttons illuminate pressed state, and the Program OLED changes on Live/type/model interactions.
Many Piano selection controls do not show selected state through their button LED/aria state, and wheel/pitch controls are focusable sliders without meaningful interaction behavior.
The live footer truthfully reports MIDI DENIED, and sample preparation catches load/decode failures and labels the mode FALLBACK · SYNTH PIANO.

The no-Web-Audio fallback is not actually playable because PianoAudioEngine.noteOn returns null when context is absent; the missing-model failure path exists only as state/display code and is not reachable from a model failure control.

audio.ts cleanly separates injectable context/sample-loader inputs, recorded sample loading, per-layer gains, shared piano bus, timbre filter, compressor, dry/wet reverb, master gain, and destination.
pianoState.ts and midi.ts are modular and the implementation manifest distinguishes recorded samples from generated impulse/fallback sources.
The architecture is incomplete relative to the claimed Piano state: several state values are not connected to the graph, and the required real audio-boundary tests are missing.
The supplied verification passed test, typecheck, lint, and build; the live desktop and narrow renders loaded without console errors/warnings, and the built artifact exists.
The engine caps voices, releases sources, clears timers, and calls allNotesOff on blur/unmount.
The voice map is keyed by MIDI note, which prevents independent same-note overlapping voices, and no direct OfflineAudioContext/performance/cleanup test proves the runtime graph behavior.

issues: Visual silhouette is materially too wide/short versus the reference; CSS uses aspect-ratio 3.71/1.
Control deck is a sparse generic approximation and lacks much of the reference's exact material/control density.
Required Phase 2 audio-boundary tests are absent; the feature matrix references implementation files instead of dedicated tests for several audio features.
Several Piano controls are state/display-only or only partially connected to audio, including layer levels, string resonance, acoustics, and meaningful unison.
Sostenuto is global rather than per-note, and MIDI sustain handling toggles instead of honoring CC up/down values.
No-Web-Audio fallback reports a fallback label but noteOn is silent when context is unavailable.
